sentences.sentence: **My Ego Sabotaged My Writing**
Illustration by Fresh Idea
Full manuscript in two months.
That was the goal.
I was on vacation in Mexico, no less, when I checked my email and saw the opportunity.
It was mid-June and the conference was happening near the beach, a perfect setting to refocus and get productive.
I immediately envisioned the success that awaited me – the admiration of my peers, the validation of a full manuscript within a short span, and the promise of publication deals.
But, my ego had other plans.
It started as a whisper, a gentle voice in my head telling me that I was an experienced writer and that this manuscript was going to be my masterpiece.
I'm sure others will be green with envy when they read it.
You're going to wow them with your unique style and compelling narrative.
But, as I began working on the manuscript, that whisper grew into a roar.
I started to believe that I was invincible, that my writing was flawless, and that I didn't need feedback or criticism.
I'd write 1,000 words in one sitting, feeling proud and accomplished, only to revise and rewrite them the next day, convinced that I was refining perfection.
But, the revisions weren't just minor tweaks; they were complete overhauls, fueled by my ego's insatiable need for validation.
The more I wrote, the more my ego suffocated my creativity.
I became convinced that every word, every sentence, and every paragraph was a reflection of my genius.
I refused to accept any suggestions or edits, fearing that they would sully my artistic vision.
My inner critic, once a helpful guide, had morphed into a cruel dictator, paralyzing me with self-doubt and fear.
It took a painful realization to snap me out of this ego-driven haze.
I'd been working on the manuscript for weeks, but it still wasn't coming together.
**What in the World is Shaking Up The Hospitality Industry?
How prepared are you for the revolution?
Once upon a time, not that long ago in the restaurant, food, and hospitality industry, the formula for success was pretty simple to grasp.
Following the formula was widely accepted as the guaranteed path to making a name for oneself and reaping the rewards that came with it.
But times have changed.
The once tried and true blueprint for success has been turned on its head, and a new wave of disruption is shaking up the hospitality industry in ways we never thought possible.
The rise of the digital age has led to a seismic shift in the way consumers interact with brands and expect personalized experiences.
Gone are the days of a simple restaurant website or a basic social media presence.
Today's consumers demand immersive and dynamic experiences that are tailored to their unique preferences and needs.
And it's not just the big chains that are being forced to adapt; even the smallest, most intimate establishments are being held to the same standards.
Gone are the days of a straightforward meal and a quick departure.
Today's consumers want to engage with the culinary process, from farm-to-table, interactive cooking classes, and immersive dining events that combine art, music, and performance with the food.
The rise of social media has also created a culture of influencers and bloggers, who are driving consumer behavior and demanding that establishments provide an Instagram-worthy experience.
Another area of upheaval is the way we think about staff and labor.
The traditional model of tipping and minimum wage is being turned on its head as cities like New York, California, and Seattle raise the minimum wage and explore new models of compensation.
This shift is forcing restaurateurs to rethink the way they manage their staff, invest in training, and rethink their labor costs.
Furthermore, sustainability and environmental concerns are becoming a major driving force in the hospitality industry.
**Gathering Input for a Stronger Vermont**
Aldo Das, November 25, 2020·3 min read
As the world awaits the results of COVID-19 vaccine clinical trials, we find ourselves in a unique moment of introspection and planning for the future.
In Vermont, we are preparing for the next phase of pandemic response and recovery.
To build a more resilient and inclusive community, it's essential that we gather input from organizations and partners across the state to determine what these groups will be.
In the coming months, Vermont will be working to establish new community-based groups that will serve as the backbone of our pandemic response.
These groups will be critical in helping to disseminate information, provide resources, and coordinate efforts to support our most vulnerable populations.
But to ensure that these groups are effective and representative of the needs of all Vermonters, we must involve the people who will be most impacted by their work.

By engaging with organizations and partners from diverse sectors, including healthcare, education, business, and non-profit communities, we can build a robust network of support that is tailored to the specific needs of our state.
This process will not only help us create more effective groups, but also foster a culture of collaboration and mutual understanding that will serve Vermont well beyond the pandemic.
Some potential partners to consider include:
- Local food banks and pantries, which have played a critical role in providing food assistance to those in need
- Community health centers, which offer essential healthcare services to underserved populations
- Small businesses and entrepreneurs, who are the backbone of our local economies
- Non-profit organizations that provide vital support services, such as housing and job training
By working together, we can create a more comprehensive and compassionate response to the pandemic, one that is grounded in the needs and experiences of our community.
This is not a task that can be undertaken by any one organization or government agency alone – it requires a collective effort and a willingness to listen and learn.
**How to Change Your Programming to Achieve the Results You Desire**
If negative thoughts turn into beliefs that determine your behavior, then the opposite holds true.
Positive thoughts and beliefs can lead to positive action.
This means we can reprogram our minds to achieve the results we desire.
The question is, how do we do it?
Reprogramming your mind is not an overnight process, but with consistent effort and the right strategies, you can break free from limiting thoughts and beliefs that hold you back.
Here are two simple yet powerful ways to reprogram your mind and do anything you set your mind to.
Reprogram Your Mind Through Self-Talk**
The way you talk to yourself matters.
Your inner dialogue has the power to shape your thoughts, emotions, and actions.
When you talk to yourself, ask yourself questions like: "What would a confident person say in this situation?"
For example, instead of saying "I'll never be able to do this," say "I can learn and grow from this experience."
By doing so, you will begin to rewire your brain with a more positive and optimistic mindset.
Reprogram Your Mind Through Visualization**
Visualization is a powerful tool that can rewire your brain and make your goals feel more achievable.
Close your eyes and vividly imagine yourself achieving your goals and succeeding in your endeavors.
Imagine the feeling of accomplishment, the sense of pride, and the joy of living a life you love.
Visualize yourself overcoming obstacles and challenges with ease and confidence.
The more you visualize, the more your brain will start to believe that your goals are achievable.
This will lead to increased motivation, determination, and a renewed sense of purpose.
By visualizing your success, you will begin to attract opportunities and resources that will help you achieve your goals.
Title: Embracing the Future of Intimacy: Why Everyone Should Consider Owning a Sex Doll
There's nothing weird about owning a sex doll.
Most of us would, if they were cheaper.
A sex doll costs about as much as a car.
I'm talking high-end models, not the inflatable ones.
Those run around a hundred bucks.
No, the ones I'm referring to are the incredibly lifelike and anatomically correct ones that can cost upwards of $10,000.
But trust me, they're worth it.
One of the main reasons sex dolls are worth considering is that they offer a solution to the growing problem of loneliness.
In today's society, it's not uncommon for people to be single for extended periods of time.
This can lead to feelings of isolation and disconnection.
Sex dolls can help alleviate these feelings by providing a companion that's always available, always interested, and always understanding.
Another benefit of sex dolls is their ability to accommodate various preferences and needs.
They come in a wide range of sizes, shapes, and features, making them suitable for people with different bodies, abilities, and orientations.
This inclusivity is something that traditional sex education and relationships often lack.
Moreover, sex dolls can help reduce stress and anxiety related to dating and relationships.
No more worrying about rejection, ghosting, or the fear of being hurt.
With a sex doll, you can have a safe and consensual experience that's tailored to your desires.
Some people might argue that owning a sex doll is dehumanizing or objectifying.
But I'd counter that argument by saying that it's actually the opposite.
A sex doll is an inanimate object, and treating it as such is a more honest and respectful approach than treating a human being like an object.
Humans are complex and messy, and they often come with expectations, judgments, and emotional baggage.
**Being My Own Advocate: A Journey of Self-Love and Empowerment**
Zion National Park in Utah.
Picture taken by yours truly.
Learning how to love me through creative writing has proven to be a powerful tool in my life.
My thoughts become more apparent, and it leads me to feel confident on my journey of self-discovery.
As I reflect on the twists and turns of life, I've come to realize the importance of being my own advocate.
For far too long, we've been conditioned to seek external validation and approval from others.
We often look to our families, friends, and society for guidance and reassurance, seeking a stamp of approval to confirm our worth.
But what happens when we're not good enough in their eyes?
What happens when we face rejection, criticism, or negativity?
I've learned that the most empowering decision I can make is to be my own advocate.
To stand up for myself, to speak my truth, and to love myself unconditionally.
It's a journey that requires courage, self-reflection, and a willingness to confront our deepest fears and insecurities.
As I walk the path of self-love and empowerment, I've come to understand that being my own advocate means:
1. **Acknowledging my strengths and weaknesses**: I've learned to celebrate my accomplishments and acknowledge areas where I need improvement.
By doing so, I've become more compassionate and understanding, not just of myself, but also of others.
2. **Setting boundaries**: I've learned to say "no" without guilt or shame.
I've set clear boundaries with others to protect my time, energy, and well-being.
3. **Speaking my truth**: I've become more confident in expressing my thoughts and feelings, even if they may be unpopular or challenging to others.
4. **Practicing self-care**: I've prioritized my physical, emotional, and mental well-being, making time for activities that nourish my mind, body, and soul.
Dear Prospect,
How do you approach the salesman that sells a particular product you find lovely?
— is it that you buy because of humour or the way he introduces the product to you when he displays part of his ethos as a salesman?
Just know that I have encountered many salesmen in the past and I truly believe that a salesman's approach is the key to successful sales.
Recently, I came across a salesman who I believe exemplifies the ideal approach.
His name is Jack, and he sells high-quality kitchen appliances.
What struck me about Jack was his unique ability to build rapport with his customers.
He didn't try to sell the product to me by using high-pressure sales tactics or cheesy sales pitches.
Instead, he took the time to understand my needs, interests, and preferences.
He asked me questions about my cooking style, the type of food I like to prepare, and even my favorite cooking techniques.
As we spoke, Jack displayed a genuine passion for the products he was selling.

He explained the features and benefits of each appliance in a clear and concise manner, but he also shared his own personal experiences and stories about how the products had helped him in his own kitchen.
His enthusiasm was infectious, and I found myself becoming more and more interested in the products.
But what really impressed me about Jack was his sense of humor.
He had a quick wit and was able to make me laugh even on a busy sales day.
He didn't try to force humor on me, but it was natural and genuine.
He made me feel at ease, and I appreciated his ability to connect with me on a personal level.
As a result of Jack's approach, I found myself becoming a loyal customer of his company.
I not only purchased the products he was selling, but I also recommended them to my friends and family.
I believe that Jack's approach is a great example of how a salesman can build trust and rapport with their customers.

Let the drama happen around you, not with you**

**The Child is The Father of Man: A Timeless Truth**
This in simple words means that the traits of childhood continue in manhood.
In other words, if we want to have better men, we must first have better children.
If we pay no attention to the child, he grows into a worthless youth and subsequently, a mediocre adult.
The famous proverb, "The Child is The Father of Man," reminds us of the profound impact that childhood experiences and upbringing have on shaping an individual's character and future.
The phrase is often attributed to the Roman philosopher, Plutarch, who emphasized the importance of nurturing the young mind.
It highlights the fact that the qualities we observe in children - such as curiosity, creativity, and courage - are the foundation upon which adulthood is built.
If these qualities are encouraged and developed during childhood, they will inevitably guide the individual through their formative years and shape their character into adulthood.
The consequences of neglecting the needs of children are far-reaching and devastating.
When children are left unguided, they often become disillusioned and disconnected from society.
They grow into individuals with low self-esteem, a lack of empathy, and a diminished sense of purpose.
This, in turn, affects not only their personal lives but also the lives of those around them, creating a ripple effect of dysfunction and dissatisfaction.
In contrast, when children are nurtured, supported, and encouraged to reach their full potential, they grow into confident, compassionate, and capable individuals.
They are better equipped to navigate the complexities of life, build strong relationships, and contribute positively to their communities.
So, what does this mean for us as individuals and as a society?
It means that we must invest time, effort, and resources into the development of our children.

We must prioritize their emotional and psychological well-being, provide them with access to quality education and healthcare, and teach them essential life skills such as empathy, self-discipline, and problem-solving.
